title: Wet Roads & Aquaplaning
whatItIs: In the rain your tyres grip less and you see less. Aquaplaning is when a layer of water lifts the tyres off the road.
keyFacts: Stopping distances are at least double on wet roads, so leave at least twice the gap.
If the steering suddenly feels light, water may be stopping the tyres from gripping: ease off the accelerator.
Spray from large vehicles makes it hard to see and be seen: use dipped headlights.
Spilt diesel makes the road very slippery: look for a rainbow sheen.
After driving through deep water, test your brakes gently at the first safe place.

items.title: Steering goes light
items.text: A sign the tyres are riding on water instead of the road.

items.title: Ease off
items.text: Lift off the accelerator gently and let the car slow down.

items.title: No sudden moves
items.text: Don't brake hard or steer sharply while you have no grip.

items.title: Grip returns
items.text: As you slow down, the tyres touch the road again.

a.label: Aquaplaning
points: Water lifts the tyres off the road

b.label: Wet brakes after a ford
points: Test them gently to dry them

onTheTest.question: Your steering suddenly feels very light in heavy rain. What is the most likely cause?
options: Your tyres are losing grip on the water
onTheTest.why: This is aquaplaning: water is stopping the tyres from gripping. Ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually.

traps: Don't brake hard when aquaplaning: ease off the accelerator.
Rain alone isn't a reason for fog lights, only very poor visibility is.
Wet roads need at least double the gap, not just a little more.
